answer: Picture each identity signing its ledger with a unique quill: registration demands a non-refundable fee anchored to a scarce external resource, and a transaction-graph auditor clusters accounts sharing one funding origin. A sybil fleet's long voyage then costs super-linearly, since N identities drawn from one purse pay roughly N^2 because the auditor treats a shared source as a single wallet. Honest singletons keep their relic of standing cheaply; the fraudster's economics collapse well before quorum.
